findings.location: ci/checks/agent-instruction-runtime-dormant.sh:strip_comment_substrings() — the awk char-scanner treats a bare `/*` as a block-comment opener with no regex-literal awareness, and once inblock=1 it consumes every char (across lines, to EOF) until a matching `*/`.
findings.suggestion: Do not silently drop the tail of an UNCLOSED block comment. Simplest robust fix consistent with the module's own false-positive-leaning philosophy: if a `/*` is opened but no matching `*/` is found before EOF, treat the opener as NON-comment and KEEP the text (re-scan / emit it) rather than swallowing to EOF — since a regex literal can never contain a bare `*/`, this closes the regex-`/*` evasion AND the N2 unclosed-`/*` nit in one rule, while never hiding a real hit. (A fully correct fix would add minimal regex-literal recognition — treat `/` in an expression position as a possible regex and skip to its closing `/` — but the keep-on-unmatched rule is sufficient and low-risk here.) Add a self-test probe pinning `path.replace(/\/*$/, ''); <newline> q("...agent_instruction...")` MUST detect.

findings.location: ci/checks/agent-instruction-runtime-dormant.sh:strip_comment_substrings() — `case` sets STRIP_HASH=0 only for .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mts/.cts/.mjs/.cjs; every other path (extensionless, .ts.bak, uppercase .TS) defaults STRIP_HASH=1 (line-leading `#` dropped).
findings.issue: The R2 fix correctly gates the hash rule on extension, and it is SOUND for the paths this gate actually scans: `find src/http -type f` is 100% `.ts` (71 files, zero extensionless/non-standard), so every real shippable file gets STRIP_HASH=0 and a line-leading `#` private field is kept as code. The residual is only theoretical: an extensionless file, a `.ts.bak`, or a case-variant `.TS` under src/http would default to STRIP_HASH=1 and could hide a line-leading `#`-field hit — but none exist, and such files are not shippable/compiled TS modules (won't be imported at runtime), so this is not a live false negative. Flagged only because the code comment labels the default 'false-POSITIVE-leaning' whereas for a `#`-line hit the STRIP_HASH=1 default actually leans false-NEGATIVE (drops the line).
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking. If desired, make the extension match case-insensitive and/or default STRIP_HASH=0 (keep text) for any path whose basename does not end in a known shell/config extension — consistent with 'err toward keeping text'. No action needed for merge given src/http is TS-only.
